subject: dragonfly
reasoning:
I'm sketching the dragonfly's proportions — a body around 8cm long with a roughly 10cm wingspan, facing forward with wings held out horizontally in a resting perched pose, legs touching the ground.

Working out the skeleton hierarchy: a thorax root with chains for the drooping abdomen, head/jaw, four hinged wings, and six three-jointed legs, then placing coordinates for each attachment point on the thorax. Still writing wing outline coordinates...

Assigning the wing joint a forward direction with a wing role, then moving to the body: a metallic green thorax, and an abdomen built from a five-segment chain tapering from a slightly swollen base down to a thin tip, with alternating blue/black color bands along its length.

Now I'm adding a jaw hinge, then building six legs as three-joint chains (hip, knee, foot) positioned under the thorax, and sweeping thin rod geometry along each chain to form the limbs.

Next I'm sizing the thorax sphere, positioning its root joint, and considering small antennae rods plus stripe coloring for the body surface.

Then I work out the head and neck joints relative to the thorax, add eye and jaw placement, and figure out the forewing and hindwing joint positions for a symmetrical, slightly layered wing attachment.

I'm setting up the wings now, slightly offsetting forewing and hindwing heights to prevent z-fighting, and planning vein rods along the leading edge and a dark pterostigma patch near the tip. I'm writing a reusable wing function that takes side, name, base height, and scale so I can mirror left and right wings consistently.

For the abdomen, I'm adding claspers as two small spikes near the tail angled slightly outward and downward, and working out a tapering radius function so the abdomen swells near the thorax and narrows toward the tip.

I'm laying out the abdomen as a slightly drooping catmull-rom path with parent chaining to the thorax joint, then sweeping bones over it with striped paint. For the head, I'm applying bone-driven sweeps to each part and giving the eyes a countershaded gradient paint for a glossy look, with the wing height set near the top of the body.

Checking the lowest point, I'm nudging the feet up to about 0.0007 so the tube caps don't poke below y=0, keeping proportions tight.
